The prototype is at **http://maker:4001/openpage.html** (screenshot `prototypes/shot-48-openpage.png`).

My proposed default for opening the original page — **several natural ways all lead there**, opening in a **new browser tab** so your bookmark library stays put:

- The **title** (shown as a link with a small ↗) opens the page.
- The **preview image** opens it (a subtle "↗ Open page" hint appears on hover).
- The **web address** opens it.
- An explicit **↗ Open page** button, for when you want an obvious control.

And things that should *not* open the page keep their own jobs: **tag pills** filter by that tag, and **Edit / Archive** do their actions.

(In this preview, "opening" shows a small confirmation toast instead of navigating away, so you can stay on the screen — in the real app it opens the actual page in a new tab.)

Two things I decided that I'd like you to weigh in on:

1. I made the page open in a **new tab** (your library stays open behind it). Does that match how you'd want it — or would you expect it to open in the *same* tab, replacing the library?
2. I made **multiple spots** open the page (title, preview, address, and a button). Is that helpful, or would you rather only an explicit **Open** control did it, so clicking the title/card could instead do something else (like expand details in place)?
